title: Fixed Inclined Beam and Suspended Warp Weight Loom
description: One newly authored complete warp-weighted upright textile loom in a single fixed display pose. Two long finite feet carry inclined full standards and independent rear braces, with a complete upper transverse winding beam and a short folded woven-cloth appearance. Twelve continuous thick warp strands descend from that cloth edge; alternate paths pass in front of a distinct low shed bar, and six complete thick perforated clay-looking weights terminate the paired hanging strands. Each weight has a genuine open upper hole and continuous whole material rim, not a painted circle. Short side brackets hold a separate projecting heddle rod and individual closed elongated heddle loops around the alternate strand lanes. Unlike the old bounded flat loom, there is no lower beam fixing the warp ends: the open lower field and independently hanging weights define the full silhouette and support relation. Unlike the fore-aft treadle loom there are no rear warp drum, floor treadles, twin castle shafts or reed-beater assembly. All coordinates authored for this one complete inclined weighted apparatus, no old frame or cloth meshes copied. Four opaque solid PBR materials, metres Z up, horizontal bounds-centred ground origin. One static cultural-craft prop zero scenes. Generic illustrative construction, no historical reconstruction, working weave, tension equilibrium, weight suspension safety, shed movement, cloth simulation, ergonomics, manufacture or safe use; rigging animation interaction not made.
